subject: Deletion SLA Q&A, execution reconciliation & audit evidence
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightmed.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightMed Security <security@brightmed.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: full deletion (prompts/outputs/logs) + Q&A on SLA and evidence

Hi Priya,

We need to initiate a full deletion request for BrightMed interaction records tied to the clinical-assist project: dataset id BM-CLIN-2024 and the tenant ID bm-health-58. This should include:
- user prompts and assistant outputs (prompt-output logs),
- inference request/response traces (ingest logs),
- any cached KV/prefix entries used for session continuation.

Questions we have before we mark this as an official erasure request:
1) What is the expected SLA (business days) from acceptance to irreversible deletion?
2) Do you provide a per-item manifest showing exactly which S3/Blob paths were deleted plus the deletion timestamps and operator identity?
3) Can you provide evidence of KMS key zeroization (if keys were used to encrypt those artifacts)?
4) Are there any artifacts that stay in cold backups or WORM (write-once) archives?

We will need a signed statement for compliance. Please outline the workflow and the minimal evidence package we should expect so our InfoSec and compliance teams can sign off. If helpful, loop in your ops/CS.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Privacy & Security
BrightMed Health

On the operational side, Jordan Blake is our internal contact for validation (he's copied on our side).
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: full deletion (prompts/outputs/logs) + Q&A on SLA and evidence

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers up front, then a concrete workflow and artefact list below.

Quick answers:
- SLA: standard execution window is 10 business days from formal intake (we can expedite to 3 business days for approved escalations).
- Manifest: yes — we provide a CSV manifest listing object paths, deletion timestamps (UTC), and operator/job ids.
- KMS zeroization: we can provide KMS key state change logs and a signed statement that the key material used for those objects is no longer accessible; direct HSM proof depends on customer-managed keys.
- Backups: objects in immutable WORM archives or 3rd-party cold backups are handled case-by-case; we will enumerate any exceptions during intake.

Proposed workflow (steps):
1) Intake: Customer completes the Erasure Request form (we will open HS-94217). We validate tenant id and dataset ids.
2) Scope & freeze: Mark affected routes/prefixes for quiesce; pause retention-based restores.
3) KV cache quiesce: Evict prefix/KV entries and snapshot eviction logs.
4) Deletion job: Run delete pipeline across object stores + index removal (multi-region where applicable).
5) Verification: Re-scan indexes and attempt sample reads to confirm 404/NotFound.
6) Manifest & signed statement: Ops generates CSV manifest + signed PDF statement and uploads to shared Drive and DocuSign.
7) Audit handoff: We provide deletion timestamps, job ids, operator ids, KMS change logs, and a short reconciliation report.

Attachments we will provide as part of the evidence package:
- redwood-erase-manifest-<date>.csv (object path, hash, deletion_ts_utc, job_id)
- kv-cache-quiesce-log-<date>.txt
- signed-deletion-statement-<tenant>.pdf

Next steps for us: Marissa (cc'd) will open the ticket and run preliminary validation. Please confirm final scope (BM-CLIN-2024 + any additional prefixes) and the legal contact for the signed statement. If you need faster turnaround we can route to expedited SLA.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightmed.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: full deletion (prompts/outputs/logs) + Q&A on SLA and evidence

Priya — opening HS-94217 now. Preliminary checklist for ops run (internal):
- Confirm tenant: bm-health-58
- Enumerate object prefixes: s3://redwood-prod/tenants/bm-health-58/prompts/, s3://redwood-prod/tenants/bm-health-58/outputs/, index db entries in ES cluster redwood-logs-prod, tracer table in redwood-traces-prod (region us-west-2)
- Check for snapshots older than 90 days in glacier-style archives.
- Lockdown: place retention flag so no inbound writes for the tenant during purge window.
- KV cache: run prefix eviction job and capture kv-cache-quiesce-log-20261128.txt
- Execute delete pipeline (dry-run first, then live) with job ids noted.

Marissa — are you able to capture the KMS key rotation/disable events for the tenant's envelope key? If the keys are customer-managed, we need to call the key owner to confirm zeroization.

I'll update HS-94217 with the exact job ids and an ETA.

—Marissa
Head of Data Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightmed.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, BrightMed Security <security@brightmed.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: full deletion (prompts/outputs/logs) + Q&A on SLA and evidence

Thanks — that workflow is clear. A couple of follow-ups from our InfoSec team:
- We need deletion evidence that includes deletion_ts, object path, and the operator/job id.
- For KMS zeroization, BrightMed uses our centrally managed key (BYOK). Our KMS owner will provide the rotation/disable logs — but please confirm you will record and include the envelope key id in the manifest.
- Can the signed statement include an explicit line that no copies remain in hot or warm storage as of the deletion timestamp?

If you can produce a sample redacted manifest and a quick note on the format, we can route it to our legal team while ops runs.

Regards,
Samir

Evidence provided (attachments & links):

Thanks — Priya
